title: Difference Between Ones and Zeros in Row and Column
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix, construct a difference matrix where each element diff[i][j] is calculated as the sum of ones in the i-th row and j-th column minus the sum of zeros in the i-th row and j-th column.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix, construct a difference matrix where each element diff[i][j] is calculated as the sum of ones in the i-th row and j-th column minus the sum of zeros in the i-th row and j-th column.
constraints: For every cell, compute row ones + column ones - row zeros - column zeros.
The cell itself participates once through its row and once through its column.
Return the full difference matrix with the same shape.
hints: Count ones once for every row and column.
Row zeros equal width-row_ones, and column zeros equal height-column_ones.
The formula is algebraically identical to the definition and fills each output cell in constant time after preprocessing.
editorial: The formula is algebraically identical to the definition and fills each output cell in constant time after preprocessing.

tests.explanation: The row has two ones and each column one, with no zeros, so both entries equal three.
